item.title: 2 people killed in Trenton, New Jersey, shooting identified
item.description: Two people died and eight others were hurt in a shooting on Locust Street in Trenton early Sunday morning, officials say.

item.title: North Carolina teen indicted in San Diego mosque shooting over livestream
item.description: A 17-year-old North Carolina girl has been charged with murder by aiding and abetting in connection with the deadly rampage at the Islamic Center of San Diego in May.

item.title: E&Y to award $100 million in bonuses for workers who show people skills
item.description: Management consulting firm EY said it will reward employees who demonstrate human skills, such as business acumen and judgment.

item.title: Watch: Flash flood sweeps through Grand Canyon
item.description: At least two people are dead, and 15 are missing after heavy rainfall triggered flash floods in the Grand Canyon over the weekend. These videos show the floodwaters in the national park and the aftermath.

item.title: Trump says more coming as U.S., Iran trade strikes for first time in weeks
item.description: President Trump says the U.S. will hit Iran hard after it targeted American bases, which Tehran said was in retaliation for U.S. attacks in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Day 3 of Lindsay Clancy trial deliberations ends without verdict
item.description: Jurors in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial went home Monday without reaching a verdict. CBS News correspondent Shanelle Kaul has the latest.

item.title: Supreme Court rules Trump's White House ballroom construction can continue
item.description: The Supreme Court ruled 5-4 on Monday that construction can continue on President Trump's White House ballroom. CBS News' Jake Rosen reports.

item.title: Ross Fire still burning after a week, with 85,000 acres scorched
item.description: The wildfire, which has torn through Palo Pinto and Jack counties, has forced evacuations, closed roads and disrupted schools.

item.title: Supreme Court continues to allow construction of Trump's White House ballroom
item.description: The Supreme Court divided 5-4 in allowing construction of the new White House ballroom to continue.

item.title: Trump inks deal with 9 pharmaceutical companies to lower drug costs
item.description: The White House said the agreements will reduce costs to treat Parkinson's disease, macular degeneration, glaucoma, liver disease and other illnesses.

item.title: FTC and 22 states sue Amazon over alleged secret ad surcharge scheme
item.description: Regulators allege that sellers and brands were overcharged by tens of billions of dollars through secretly inflated ad prices.

item.title: Trump pushing communities to accept data centers
item.description: President Trump posted on social media Monday that people who "want to be successful and rich" should be supporting data centers. CBS News' Weijia Jiang reports.

item.title: House returns with vote expected to prevent government shutdown
item.description: The House is back in session after a five-week recess with a vote expected on a Senate-passed, short-term funding bill to keep the government open. CBS News' Taurean Small has more.

item.title: 2 dead, about 15 missing after Grand Canyon hit by flash floods
item.description: Violent flash floods hit the Grand Canyon's Bright Angel Canyon and Phantom Ranch area, the National Park Service said, leaving more than a dozen people missing.

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed's deleted tweets on 9/11 invite scrutiny of past remarks
item.description: Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed deleted posts invoking 9/11 and the U.S. response.

item.title: What's a good money market account rate considered to be this September?
item.description: Thinking of moving some money into a market account? Here's what a good rate on the account is considered to be now.

item.title: 3 reasons why debt relief could be worth pursuing this September
item.description: This September could usher in challenges for borrowers who are already struggling to make progress on their debt.

item.title: What sparked the latest U.S. strikes against Iran
item.description: The U.S. and Iran traded strikes over the weekend for the first time in a month. The attacks came after President Trump hit Iran with new sanctions. CBS News national security analyst Aaron MacLean has more.

item.title: Tropical storm warning issued along Louisiana, Texas coasts
item.description: The National Hurricane Center issued a tropical storm warning for coastal Texas and Louisiana on Monday as a tropical depression formed in the Gulf.

item.title: Kalshi bans ex-congressman George Santos for life after suspicious trades
item.description: George Santos faces a lifetime ban from Kalshi after failing to cooperate with the prediction market's investigation into his alleged unlawful trades.

item.title: Judge orders National Guard shooting suspect to be force-fed
item.description: Rahmanullah Lakanwal, accused last year of fatally shooting a National Guard member and severely injuring another, has been refusing to eat for months while in government custody.

item.title: Lionel Messi says he is retiring from the Argentina national soccer team
item.description: Lionel Messi played in six World Cups and led Argentina to win the tournament in 2022 in Qatar.

item.title: Kalshi official reacts to oversight ruling against company
item.description: Robert DeNault, head of enforcement at Kalshi, joins CBS News to discuss last week's appeals court ruling that rejected the company's efforts to stop Nevada from regulating speculation on sporting events on its platform.

item.title: Will Trump's Venezuela oil deal ease U.S. gas prices?
item.description: The deal involves developing 17 strategic oil fields in Venezuela, an undertaking that experts said could take years.

item.title: Expert says Americans won't see changes at gas pump "anytime soon" as Trump touts Venezuela deal
item.description: Michael Noel, an economics professor at Texas Tech University, joins CBS News 24/7 to discuss the Trump administration's deal with Venezuela, and if it will actually provide any relief at the gas pump.

item.title: John Galliano's Met Gala exhibit canceled amid backlash
item.description: The Met's decision to highlight the work by designer John Galliano sparked widespread controversy due to his history of antisemitic and racist comments.

item.title: House returns with vote expected on Senate bill to prevent shutdown
item.description: Lawmakers could also vote on condemning socialism and censuring GOP Rep. Chuck Edwards.

item.title: Moving Through Grief
item.description: August is National Grief Awareness Month, and Kate Doerge wants to reimagine how we deal with grief. After the experience of losing her 16-year-old daughter, Kate decided it was time to reframe the feeling of sadness. We've all heard of the five stages of grief, but Kate suggests there are five actions to help you learn how to carry your grief. Plus, Norah talks about how she wants to be remembered, and Kate tells us how to show up for people who are grieving.

item.title: Exercise: Your Insurance Policy for the Future
item.description: In this episode of Healthful, Norah O'Donnell is joined by her personal trainer and fitness expert, Kira Stokes. Since they started exercising together 12 years ago, Kira pushed Norah to lift heavier weights - something Norah initially resisted. Norah has since learned that you lose up to 8-percent of your muscle mass every decade after the age of 30. The two discuss the emotional connection between movement and mental health, how to get started exercising, and what about those weighted vests! Plus - Norah answers what her favorite and least favorite exercises are. We'd love to hear what topics you want to hear covered on Healthful. Text Norah at 202-217-1107.

item.title: The Gut-Brain Secret: What Your Body Knows Before You Do
item.description: Numerous diseases may be traceable back to the gut—from depression and anxiety to Parkinson's disease—and for many people, "food is medicine" is a compelling concept. Dr. Trisha Pasricha is a world-leading expert on the gut-brain connection. On this episode of Healthful, she and Norah discuss what role food can play in treating disease. They also cover why more women suffer from irritable bowel syndrome than men, the impact hormones and antibiotics have on your digestive system, and what to know about the ongoing Cyclospora outbreak.
